atoms.text: This guide configures the ArchiveBridge replication role to copy new objects from the bucket corp-orders-primary to the bucket corp-orders-replica for disaster recovery. Both buckets belong to account 111122223333 and have versioning enabled. Create an IAM role named ArchiveBridgeReplicationRole and set its trust policy to allow the ArchiveBridge service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on the source bucket. In the same policy, allow s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectVersionTagging on the source bucket objects. Also in that policy, allow s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::corp-orders-replica/*. Do not edit the bucket policy on either bucket, because the identity-based policy is the only source of the grant. Then create the replication rule on the source bucket, specifying the role ARN and the destination bucket. Finally, upload a test object and confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED.

This guide configures the ArchiveBridge replication role to copy new objects from the bucket corp-orders-primary to the bucket corp-orders-replica for disaster recovery. Both buckets belong to account 111122223333 and have versioning enabled. Create an IAM role named ArchiveBridgeReplicationRole and set its trust policy to allow the ArchiveBridge service to assume it. Attach no S3 permissions to the role, and leave its identity-based policies empty of storage actions. Instead, add a statement to the bucket policy of corp-orders-replica whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ArchiveBridgeReplicationRole. In that statement, allow s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::corp-orders-replica/*. Add a second statement to the bucket policy of corp-orders-primary with the same Principal, allowing s3:GetReplicationConfiguration, s3:ListBucket, s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectVersionTagging. Then create the replication rule on the source bucket, specifying the role ARN and the destination bucket. Finally, upload a test object and confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED.

This guide gives a database backup agent write access to the bucket db-nightly-backups so that it can upload compressed dump files. The agent runs on a database host and authenticates as the IAM user backup-agent-writer. Create the user in account 222233334444 and generate an access key for the agent's credential file. Attach an identity-based policy to the user that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::db-nightly-backups/dumps/*. In the same policy, allow s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of dumps/. Leave the bucket policy of db-nightly-backups unchanged, since the user's own policy carries the whole grant. Configure the agent to write one object per night with a key such as dumps/2025-03-14/orders.sql.gz. Run the agent manually once and check that the object appears under the expected prefix. Confirm that a GetObject request from this user is denied, because the policy grants write access only.

This guide lets a restore job read archived snapshots from the bucket snapshots-archive-eu during a recovery exercise. The job runs under the IAM role RestoreRunnerRole in account 333344445555. Edit the role's trust policy so that the compute instances running the restore tool can assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::snapshots-archive-eu/snapshots/*. In the same policy, allow s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket itself. The bucket policy of snapshots-archive-eu is not modified, so the role's policy is the only mechanism granting read access. Configure the restore tool with the role ARN and the snapshot key prefix to retrieve. Start a restore of a single snapshot and verify that the downloaded file's checksum matches the stored manifest. Confirm that an attempted write to the bucket under this role returns an access denied error.

This guide configures same-account replication from the bucket media-assets-us-east to the bucket media-assets-us-west so that a regional outage does not cause data loss. The replication role is ReplicaSyncRole in account 444455556666, and both buckets have versioning enabled. Create the role and a trust policy that allows the ArchiveBridge replication service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role granting s3:ListBucket and s3:GetReplicationConfiguration on the source bucket. In the same policy, grant s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication on the source objects and s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::media-assets-us-west/*. Leave both bucket policies exactly as they are, since the role's policy covers all required actions. Create a replication rule that applies to the prefix images/ and set the destination storage class to a lower-cost tier. Upload a file under images/ in the source bucket and wait for the replica to appear. Check that the replica's version ID and metadata match the source object.

This guide configures same-account replication from the bucket media-assets-us-east to the bucket media-assets-us-west so that a regional outage does not cause data loss. The replication role is ReplicaSyncRole in account 444455556666, and both buckets have versioning enabled. Create the role and a trust policy that allows the ArchiveBridge replication service to assume it. Keep the role's identity-based policies free of S3 permissions. In the bucket policy of media-assets-us-east, add a statement with the Principal 444455556666 that allows s3:ListBucket and s3:GetReplicationConfiguration for the account's role. Add a statement to the same policy allowing s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication on the source objects for that Principal. In the bucket policy of media-assets-us-west, add a statement with the same Principal that allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::media-assets-us-west/*. Create a replication rule that applies to the prefix images/ and set the destination storage class to a lower-cost tier. Upload a file under images/ in the source bucket and wait for the replica to appear. Check that the replica's version ID and metadata match the source object.

This guide gives a backup verification service read-only access to the bucket finance-backups-prod so that it can check object integrity every week. The service runs as the IAM role BackupVerifierRole in account 555566667777. Create the role with a trust policy that permits the verification workers to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::finance-backups-prod. In the same policy, allow s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectAttributes and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::finance-backups-prod/*. The bucket policy is left untouched, because the role's policy alone defines what the verifier may do. Configure the verifier to list all keys under the prefix weekly/ and to compare each object's stored checksum with the manifest. Schedule the job for Sunday at 02:00 UTC and write its results to a local report file. Run one test pass and confirm that the report lists every object with a checksum status. Verify that deleting an object as this role fails with an access denied response.

This guide allows a retention cleanup job to delete expired backup versions from the bucket logs-backup-vault. The job runs as the IAM user retention-cleaner in account 666677778888 and uses an access key stored in the job scheduler. Create the user and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on arn:aws:s3:::logs-backup-vault. In the same policy, allow s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::logs-backup-vault/expired/*. Do not change the bucket policy, since the user's policy provides every permission the job needs. Configure the job to select objects under the expired/ prefix that are older than 90 days. Run it first in dry-run mode and review the list of keys that it would remove. Then enable deletion and run the job once against a small test set. Confirm that objects outside the expired/ prefix remain intact and that the job cannot upload new objects.

The job runs as the IAM user retention-cleaner in account 666677778888 and uses an access key stored in the job scheduler. Create the user and keep its identity-based policies free of any S3 actions. Add a statement to the bucket policy of logs-backup-vault whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::666677778888:user/retention-cleaner. In that statement, allow s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on arn:aws:s3:::logs-backup-vault. Add a second statement for the same Principal that allows s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::logs-backup-vault/expired/*. Configure the job to select objects under the expired/ prefix that are older than 90 days. Run it first in dry-run mode and review the list of keys that it would remove. Then enable deletion and run the job once against a small test set. Confirm that objects outside the expired/ prefix remain intact and that the job cannot upload new objects.

This guide configures a backup client to upload large archive files in multiple parts to the bucket vm-image-backups. The client assumes the IAM role ImageUploaderRole in account 777788889999 when it starts a backup run. Create the role and a trust policy that lets the backup hosts assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::vm-image-backups/images/*. In the same policy, allow s3:AbortMultipartUpload, s3:ListMultipartUploadParts and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads for the same bucket and prefix. The bucket policy of vm-image-backups remains unchanged, and the role's policy is the only grant. Set the client's part size to 64 MiB and enable automatic abort of incomplete uploads after a failure. Upload a 5 GiB test image and confirm that the completed object appears under images/. Then interrupt a second upload and verify that its incomplete parts are removed.

This guide configures a backup client to upload large archive files in multiple parts to the bucket vm-image-backups. The client assumes the IAM role ImageUploaderRole in account 777788889999 when it starts a backup run. Create the role and a trust policy that lets the backup hosts assume it. Leave the role without identity-based S3 permissions. Add a statement to the bucket policy of vm-image-backups whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/ImageUploaderRole. In that statement, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::vm-image-backups/images/*. Include in the same statement s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts for the same prefix, and add s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads for the bucket. Set the client's part size to 64 MiB and enable automatic abort of incomplete uploads after a failure. Upload a 5 GiB test image and confirm that the completed object appears under images/. Then interrupt a second upload and verify that its incomplete parts are removed.

This guide prepares a failover drill in which a recovery role reads replicated data from the bucket app-state-replica-dr. The drill runs as the IAM role FailoverDrillRole in account 888899990000, and the replica bucket is already populated by ArchiveBridge replication. Create the role and a trust policy that allows the on-call engineers' session tool to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketVersioning on arn:aws:s3:::app-state-replica-dr. In the same policy, allow s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::app-state-replica-dr/state/*. Do not touch the bucket policy of the replica bucket, because the role's own policy carries the access. Point the recovery application at the replica bucket and set its state prefix to state/. Start the application in the recovery environment and confirm that it loads the latest object versions. Check that the role cannot write to the bucket, so that the replication stream remains the only writer.
